title: How a bank statement becomes data
description: A step-by-step walk through the OCR pipeline I worked on, from PDF upload to Excel export.
transcript: The video has no sound. A diagram lights up one step at a time:
1. A statement arrives as a PDF.
2. The detector picks the bank layout.
3. Known layouts go to the positional extractor, which reads PdfPig word boxes.
4. Unclear pages fall back to Gemini.
5. Every row is validated and de-duplicated (balances and signs).
6. Clean transactions export to an Excel workbook (EPPlus).

title: Lehman's laws in under 30 seconds
description: The eight laws of software evolution, one card each.
transcript: The video has no sound. Each of Lehman's eight laws gets one card:
I. Continuing change: a system in real use must keep changing, or it becomes less useful.
II. Increasing complexity: as a system changes, its complexity grows unless work is done to reduce it.
III. Self-regulation: system evolution is self-regulating, with trends that can be measured.
IV. Conservation of organisational stability: the average rate of work on an evolving system stays roughly constant.
V. Conservation of familiarity: the amount of change in each release stays roughly constant over time.
VI. Continuing growth: functional content must keep growing to keep users satisfied.
VII. Declining quality: quality appears to decline unless the system is adapted to its environment.
VIII. Feedback system: evolution processes are multi-level, multi-loop feedback systems.
